thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Sylvan Health (dedicated-pool 'sylvan-prod') canary failure rate spike detected. 5xx rate > 6% over 3m. Autoscroll: canary slice = 10%.

lina: Paging oncall (I have the page). Jumping in — checking cluster metrics and canary logs.

lina: quick summary for everyone: canary started at 04:10 UTC, at ~04:22 we started seeing elevated 5xx for the canary traffic. Impact isolated to Sylvan dedicated pool canary slice.

ryan: on the way. seeing similar in the dashboard — latency + errored token spikes. Any recent artifact rollouts?

marta: FYI, we pushed a quantized artifact (sha: 9f2a7c1) to canary at 03:58 as part of scheduled rollout. Stable pool is still on 7b4d3a2.

lina: good catch. Logs show OOM-ish patterns and KV cache misses around the same timeframe.

alex: pinging Sylvan SRE (cc @carmen) — customer reported increased error rates at 04:25 on their end. They have live traffic in canary.

carmen: we got a page from Sylvan via pagerduty at 04:27, they can still hit stable pool fine. Can confirm customer is on-call and standing by for mitigation.

lina: immediate plan: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% 2) pin Sylvan to stable artifact 7b4d3a2 3) if needed, quarantine canary nodes / evacuate tenant routing 4) coordinate with Sylvan for postmortem.

ryan: agree. I can apply the traffic freeze and pin. Lina — can you do the handoff to me? I'm taking over incident.

lina: handing off to @ryan. I'm staying for 10 more mins for context then will go to follow-up doc.

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: oncall_handoff from lina -> ryan at 04:34 UTC.

ryan: executing step 1 — reducing canary fraction for sylvan-prod to 0%.

deploy-bot: Command received: `redwoodctl traffic set --tenant sylvan --env prod --slice canary --percent 0`

deploy-bot: Result: SUCCESS. Canary slice set to 0% for sylvan-prod.

ryan: verifying traffic distribution... metrics show canary qps -> 0, stable qps absorbing traffic. Error rate on customer requests dropping in last 45s.

marta: prepping pin command. Artifact pinning will ensure traffic uses the stable artifact across pools.

ryan: pinning artifact to 7b4d3a2 (stable). Running:
```
redwoodctl artifact pin --tenant sylvan --env prod --artifact 7b4d3a2 --reason "canary failure, emergency pin"
```

deploy-bot: Command received: `redwoodctl artifact pin --tenant sylvan --env prod --artifact 7b4d3a2 --reason "canary failure, emergency pin"`

deploy-bot: Result: SUCCESS. Artifact 7b4d3a2 pinned for tenant sylvan in prod.

lina: nice. Two quick asks: 1) do we quarantine the canary nodes to avoid future automatic retries? 2) if we revert the artifact on canary pool, do we want to repro locally first?

ryan: quarantine yes — mark the canary nodegroup as no-new-traffic and start eviction of in-flight requests where safe. I'll run the script to cordon/evict.

marta: note — this pool has a custom kernel config. If we revert to older artifact we must ensure model binary compatibility. I'd prefer we route all tenant traffic to stable and then repro the quantized build in a staging cluster.

carmen: I've briefed Sylvan SRE: they're OK with pin-to-stable and a short maintenance window to investigate. They asked for timeline and confirmation once traffic fully off canary.

ryan: cordoning canary nodegroup now.

deploy-bot: Command received: `redwoodctl node cordon --nodegroup sylvan-canary-az1`

deploy-bot: Result: SUCCESS. Nodegroup sylvan-canary-az1 cordoned.

ryan: eviction started. Using graceful timeout 30s.

lina: monitoring logs — 5xx rate for Sylvan requests now down to 0.8% across stable. Good.

ryan: starting post-facto artifact rollback on canary pool to avoid automated retry bringing the bad artifact back. But since artifact already pinned for tenant, this is just defensive. Command:
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --nodegroup sylvan-canary-az1 --artifact 7b4d3a2 --force
```

deploy-bot: Command received: `redwoodctl deploy rollback --nodegroup sylvan-canary-az1 --artifact 7b4d3a2 --force`

deploy-bot: Result: SUCCESS. Can confirm nodegroup sylvan-canary-az1 now runs artifact 7b4d3a2.

marta: I'll add a temporary autoscale rule to keep canary capacity minimized until we sign off.

ryan: quick customer impact assessment: ~12k requests/min at peak for Sylvan; approx 30% of their canary traffic saw 5xx during spike window. No data exfiltration or permission issues indicated. Latency spike for prompt generation averaged +400ms.

carmen: Sylvan ops wants a post-incident call at 09:00 their local time (13:00 UTC). I'll schedule and include logs + trace links.

lina: adding runbook + artifacts to followup doc. Also flagging eval regression queue for the quantized build.

ryan: next steps for us: 1) keep Sylvan pinned to stable 7b4d3a2 for 24h 2) repro quantized build in staging with Sylvan-like load 3) run memory profiling and KV cache analysis 4) prepare rollback-capable canary strategy (smaller fraction, health probe changes).

incident-bot: INCIDENT: severity P2 -> Mitigated (customer traffic routed off canary and artifact pinned).

lina: handing incident fully to ryan for follow-up and postmortem. Thanks team. I'll join the postmortem doc later. :thumbsup:

ryan: taking ownership. Will update the incident timeline and tag the change in the release notes.

carmen: confirmed Sylvan notified. They reported traffic normalized.

marta: I'll open an internal ticket to look at our quantized build pipeline for edge-case memory regressions.

ryan: logging the mitigation steps to the incident tracker: traffic freeze -> artifact pin -> node cordon -> rollback -> confirm stable. Will attach traces + flame graphs.

deploy-bot: NOTE: audit entry created: action=artifact_pin actor=ryan artifact=7b4d3a2 tenant=sylvan time=04:39 UTC

lina: closing slack thread for live mitigation. All follow-ups in the incident tracker: INC-2026-1184.

incident-bot: THREAD_CLOSED: 2536004321 at 04:45 UTC
